options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.tooltip: Anti-aliasing is unavailable while Improved Transparency is on. Turn that option off to switch modes. Current mode: %1$s. %2$s
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.off.sum: Leaves the image untouched. Use it for vanilla rendering, comparisons, or when you want zero extra processing. Benefit: the cleanest baseline for testing and the least chance of blur or artifacts.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.fxaa.su: Uses a fast post-process edge filter. Use it when you want a lightweight smoothness boost with very little setup. Benefit: low performance cost and broad compatibility.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.msaa.su: Samples polygon edges multiple times before the image is resolved. Use it when you want cleaner hard geometry edges and can spare some GPU time. Benefit: sharper edge cleanup with less texture blur than post-process AA.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.ssaa.su: Renders the scene above native resolution and downsamples it. Use it when you want brute-force image quality and have plenty of performance headroom. Benefit: excellent edge cleanup and very stable detail.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.smaa.su: Detects edge patterns and blends along them more carefully than FXAA. Use it when you want stronger smoothing without as much softness. Benefit: cleaner diagonals and better detail retention.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.taa.sum: Blends current and previous frames to calm shimmering over time. Use it when thin detail flickers or distant edges crawl during motion. Benefit: the steadiest image on moving scenes and fine geometry.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.nis_sha: Adds a sharpen pass after rendering. Use it when the scene feels a little soft and you want extra crispness without changing resolution. Benefit: punchier detail and stronger local contrast.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.nis_ups: Renders below native resolution, scales back up, and sharpens the result. Use it when you want more FPS while keeping the image crisp. Benefit: strong performance gains with clear-looking output.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.fsr1_up: Renders below native resolution and reconstructs the image with edge-aware scaling. Use it when you want a balanced performance boost with cleaner edges than plain upscaling. Benefit: better detail reconstruction at lower internal resolutions.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.fsr1_rc: Upscales with FSR1 and then adds adaptive sharpening. Use it when you want the FSR1 speedup with a punchier final image. Benefit: clearer textures and edges than base FSR1 alone.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.sharpness.to: Controls how strongly the sharpen pass boosts local contrast. Use lower values for a softer natural look and higher values for extra crispness. Too much can create halos or crunchy detail.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.msaa_samples: Sets how many samples MSAA uses on polygon edges. Higher values smooth hard edges better, but they also cost more GPU time. The renderer may fall back to your GPU's maximum supported sample count.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.ssaa_scale.t: Sets how far above native resolution SSAA renders before downsampling. Higher values give the cleanest image, but they are also the most expensive. Use this when you want to trade performance for image quality.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.upscale_qual: Chooses the internal render scale for NIS Upscale, FSR1 Upscale, and FSR1 + RCAS. Quality stays closer to native resolution, while lower presets trade image fidelity for more FPS. Use it to pick the balance you want between sharpness and speed.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.nis_upscale_: Controls the render scale for NIS Upscale. Higher presets stay sharper, while lower presets push performance harder. Use it when you want to fine-tune the balance between FPS and clarity.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.fsr1_upscale: Controls the render scale for the FSR1-based modes. Higher presets stay closer to native quality, while lower presets favor speed. Use it to decide how aggressive the upscale should be.
